# Framework compatibility

Choose a specific framework, bridge and configuration. These are partial, versioned qualifications at the AG-UI boundary. A passing capability applies only to its named scenario and evidence stages.

Last qualified records import historical [#844](https://github.com/liveloveapp/hashbrown/pull/844) proof; the dates below describe that retained qualification, not a new execution. React and Angular share this evidence inventory; their display capabilities are recorded separately. Canonical consumer restore does not establish browser reload, reconnect or durable backend restart.

## Recorded run health

Static as-of snapshot of the reviewed qualification record, not a real-time status. Status: <code>not-run</code>. Historical qualifications are not the result of a new execution attempt.

The [weekly baseline workflow](https://github.com/liveloveapp/hashbrown/blob/main/.github/workflows/framework-compatibility.yml) is configured to run on main after the workflow is enabled, covering the seven approved pinned Node profiles. Candidate execution has not run and requires approved dependency/runtime constraints. Weekly attempts do not rewrite reviewed last qualified claims. This page does not claim a new weekly run exists or passed.

## Reading the states

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| passed | Required scenario stages passed for this exact configuration. |
| recipe-required | Native enrichment gap; does not mean a recipe was tested. An executed recipe needs its own versioned profile and evidence. |
| missing-upstream | Retained execution demonstrates a producer or bridge gap. |
| unsupported | Authoritatively absent capability; a failed probe alone is insufficient. |
| not-tested | No sufficient execution evidence; includes all planned coverage. |
| deferred | Intentionally outside this delivery. |

## Retained producer gaps

### langgraph: failed-tool-result

State: <code>missing-upstream</code>. A handled ToolNode error reaches MESSAGES&#95;SNAPSHOT as a tool error, but this bridge emits no TOOL&#95;CALL&#95;RESULT for the failure.

### langgraph: cancelled-outcome

State: <code>missing-upstream</code>. Public abortRun reaches the real blocked tool via the injected SDK seam; terminal RUN&#95;FINISHED has no cancelled outcome. Real API-server cancellation is not tested.

### mastra: failed-tool-outcome

State: <code>missing-upstream</code>. The real failure is JSON error text inside TOOL&#95;CALL&#95;RESULT.content with no top-level error marker. Hashbrown must not infer failure by parsing human-readable result bodies. This gap concerns ordinary foreground tools; the separately tested native background profile does supply a failed activity status and error text.

### langgraph: attributed-subagents

State: <code>missing-upstream</code>. A real compiled child StateGraph executes a ToolNode, with actual in-memory checkpoint history through the labeled SDK seam. The pinned bridge emits ordinary calls without SUBAGENT lifecycle events or subagentRunId. This is not API-server or native durable restore evidence.

### mastra: attributed-subagents

State: <code>missing-upstream</code>. The native agents configuration executes agent-worker and its real child model. The tool result supplies a subAgentThreadId inside JSON content, but the pinned bridge emits no SUBAGENT lifecycle or subagentRunId. That payload is retained verbatim; it does not establish AG-UI ownership.

### langgraph: native-activities

State: <code>recipe-required</code>. A real native dispatchCustomEvent progress probe in langgraph.spec.mjs reaches the published bridge as CUSTOM weather-progress events, without ACTIVITY&#95;SNAPSHOT/DELTA. A separate explicit producer recipe is needed for standard activity display; none is invented here.

## Scenario catalog

### Conversation and streaming

#### conversation.streaming

Text deltas arrive before completion with independent message identity.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### conversation.history

Multi-turn input preserves native message history.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>next-request</code>.

#### conversation.abnormal-eof

Consumer fault injection closes a stream without a terminal event and verifies bounded settlement; this does not claim a producer emits malformed output.

Required stages: <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

### Server and client tools

#### tools.server-execution

Actual server tool callbacks execute and emit retained wire events.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>.

#### tools.react-display

React renders retained server calls through the production browser host.

Required stages: <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>.

#### tools.angular-display

Angular renders retained server calls through the production browser host.

Required stages: <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### tools.same-name-client-inert

Explicitly classified server calls do not execute a matching client handler; independent client control runs once.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### tools.live-start

A causal execution gate establishes START before tool completion.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>.

#### tools.client-roundtrip

An independent ordinary client tool executes once and its actual result reaches the next native framework turn.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>next-request</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### tools.failure

A real tool callback fails; explicit error classification survives bridge and consumer projection without parsing human-readable result text.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### tools.cancel

Cancel actual gated tool execution and assert explicit terminal outcome and absence of late side effects; stream closure alone is insufficient.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

### Approval and control

#### approvals.resume

Allow, deny, cancel and resume preserve ownership without duplicate side effects.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

### Shared state

#### state.snapshot-patch

Snapshots and ordered patches remain isolated between threads.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>.

### Structured output

#### structured-output.schema

Complete and partial schema-constrained data are validated independently from backend object production.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

### Trusted generative UI

#### trusted-ui.components

Only trusted components with validated props render, including restore and cancellation.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

### Media and attachments

#### media.typed-history

Typed media input/history survives bridge transport with asset cleanup; no perception or file-search claim.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>.

### Activities and rich steps

#### activities.native

Native activity snapshots and deltas preserve status and content.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### activities.citations

Source, citation and attribution data survive projection.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### activities.live-start

Activity arrives at the causal gate before real tool completion.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>.

### Subagents and delegation

#### delegation.attributed-subagents

Real child execution also supplies standard lifecycle and explicit ownership provenance.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### delegation.native-child

Native child executes; this alone does not establish attributed subagent lifecycle.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>.

### Recovery and isolation

#### recovery.canonical-consumer-restore

Prepared root-store projection survives commit, JSON restore and the next outgoing request. This does not prove backend restart.

Required stages: <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>canonical-persistence</code>, <code>next-request</code>.

#### recovery.native-checkpoint

A second actual backend process restores durable server state; consumer JSON restore is insufficient.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>native-recovery</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>.

#### recovery.thread-isolation

Two concurrent threads do not mix outputs or dispatch across owners.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### recovery.browser-reload

Reload the actual browser host, restore committed display and preserve application handler counts; this does not prove native backend restart.

Required stages: <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>canonical-persistence</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

#### recovery.reconnect

Disconnect and reconnect an actual streaming subscriber, retaining ownership without duplicate tool dispatch or mixed run identity.

Required stages: <code>producer-execution</code>, <code>bridge-wire</code>, <code>core-consumer</code>, <code>browser-react</code>, <code>browser-angular</code>.

The [reviewed registry](https://github.com/liveloveapp/hashbrown/tree/main/tools/conformance/agent-frameworks/program) contains the catalog and qualification records. Producer captures and assertion sources above link to the immutable qualification commit, with retained SHA-256 hashes. New registry files are not claimed to exist at that historical commit.

Validate and reproduce the checked-in projection without installing frameworks:

```sh
node --test tools/conformance/agent-frameworks/program/*.spec.mjs
node tools/conformance/agent-frameworks/program/report.mjs --check
```

Capture regeneration and qualification promotion require an explicit reviewed change. Durable checked-in captures and source assertions support these records; this page does not rely solely on expiring CI artifacts.
